title: The Operations Process
coreMove: Synchronize resources, assumptions, trade-offs, and contingencies so the plan can move under real conditions.
sourcePressure: Core process three: operations links strategy and people through fast budgeting, synchronization, sound assumptions, operating plans, trade-offs, contingencies, quarterly reviews, and goals. No chapter-specific operating case is frozen.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reduce operations to scheduling, productivity, or budget administration.

hook: the the operations process that nobody sees until it is too late
a meeting room where every plan sounds good
a generic promise colliding with reality
counterintuition: Most leaders think X, but the opposite is true
The problem is not effort, it is discipline
Execution is not about working harder
tryThisNow: set a timer and write three priorities
audit one goal in your notebook
ask yourself what matters most today
examples: generic project kickoff with vague owners
student team with a deadline and no specificity
family calendar scene used as a management analogy

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional home-care provider building the next quarter schedule around nurse availability and referral growth
exampleSpecs.stakes: clients can be accepted faster than visits can be staffed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rachel synchronizes referral targets, nurse availability, travel time, and budget before accepting the quarter goal
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The wall map shows rural roads in gray while Rachel moves colored pins for nurse visits.

exampleSpecs.domain: a specialty bicycle manufacturer preparing a spring production run with uncertain component shipments
exampleSpecs.stakes: missed assumptions about forks and drivetrains can idle the line
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Julien asks which assumption would break the spring run first and turns it into a contingency trigger
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Which missing part stops the spring run first: forks, drivetrains, or the paint booth slot?

exampleSpecs.domain: a city arts festival coordinating permits, security, stage crews, and sponsor obligations
exampleSpecs.stakes: parallel effort can still fail if the dependencies are not synchronized
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marco makes each department state the dependency it needs from another before the operating plan is approved
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Name the handoff you need before you name your task," Marco says, closing the permit folder.

exampleSpecs.domain: a university research center dividing grant money between lab equipment, fellows, and fieldwork
exampleSpecs.stakes: refusing trade-offs can starve all three priorities
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Mikkel forces the trade-off by moving dollar amounts across the operating plan until one priority has to shrink
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 3:47 p.m., Mikkel drags the fieldwork line down and watches the equipment quote turn green.

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional grocery distributor planning holiday cold-chain capacity under uncertain demand
exampleSpecs.stakes: one warm dock can ruin inventory and customer trust
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Petra traces last holiday's spoilage to assumptions that were not reviewed quarterly and writes a contingency into the new plan
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Petra one spoiled pallet of yogurt to respect the old assumption column.
mustAvoid: generic warehouse scene repeated from culture chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: a Tokyo game localization team planning release dates across translation, QA, voice pickup, and platform submission
exampleSpecs.stakes: a missed platform submission can move the global release by weeks
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Akira turns independent task lists into one synchronized operating calendar with contingencies for voice pickup and QA defects
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You see four task lists, and Akira sees one release date that all four can quietly break.

skillTargets: test assumptions behind budgets and goals
analyze contingency and quarterly-review moves that keep operations alive

tryThisNowSpec: Write one operating assumption beside the trigger that would make you revise the plan before the next review.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
